result.title: The Dark Matter of Clinical Data: An Identification Limit on Disentangling Physiology from Care Process in electronic health records
result.comment: 24 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Supplementary Information and code are provided as ancillary files. Interactive companion with narrated explainers: https://criticaldata.github.io/Dark_Matter/
result.summary: Representations learned from electronic health record (EHR) data encode patient physiology together with the clinical process that decides what is measured, when, and for whom. We formalize the data-generating process with latent physiology, ordering intent, laboratory values that exist only when measured, a learned representation, and clinical environments, and analyze two strategies for undoing this entanglement. First, no division of the information carried by laboratory "value" and "ordering" channels is identified from a single dataset: when ordering depends on the analyte, its distribution among untested patients is not recoverable, and a sentinel code for the undefined recorded value makes it carry all the entropy of the ordering indicator, fixing partial information decomposition (PID) for every redundancy measure satisfying the Williams-Beer axioms and invariant under injective re-encoding. Second, cross-site invariance of representation-conditional outcomes is a falsifiable implication of biological invariance taken jointly with exclusion and representation-sufficiency conditions, but not an identification strategy: we construct observationally equivalent models that disagree about biological invariance, whether the invariance test fails or passes. For binary physiology this happens exactly when case mix differs, the representation is lossy, and physiology affects the outcome. A worked example yields a 9.6-percentage-point cross-site gap under an unchanged biological mechanism. Tests performed for every patient remove the ordering gate, and measured tests can restore identification: biological invariance is identified when a test exactly summarizes outcome-relevant physiology, or, for binary physiology, when two tests with independent errors are available at sites with different case mix. Cross-site analyses should be reported as tests of a stated joint hypothesis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 EHR 数据生成过程形式化为「潜在生理状态 + 决定何时测量谁的护理流程 + 仅在测量时存在的检验值 + 学习到的表示」，证明单一数据集无法识别检验数值与开单渠道的信息划分，并论证跨站点不变性只是可反驳的联合假设推论而非识别策略，同时给出可恢复识别的条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其潜在状态与观测流程纠缠、表示充分性和观察等价构造，可能为 LVR 中「latent 内容是否真正承载视觉证据」以及跨数据集探针/不变性检验能否支持因果结论提供概念参照，可供核查。
